clue.text: It's in March? All wrong, son

definitions.text: It's in March? All wrong, son

indicators.note: all wrong says the letters of the preceding words are in the wrong order and must be rearranged

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for son in family trees

explanation.surface: A parent gently correcting a child who has muddled the date of a festival.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange IT'S and MARCH to get CHRISTMA, then add S. The whole clue is also the meaning: anyone saying the festival is in March has it all wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: The festival falls in December, so placing it in spring is a mistake the whole sentence corrects.

clue.text: Smack clubs supplied to yob

parts.note: C is the card-playing abbreviation for the suit of clubs
a lout is a boorish, loutish young man

explanation.surface: A thug is given clubs to hit people with.
explanation.definitionFit: A clout is a heavy blow with the hand, just like a smack.

clue.text: First to go in very much like a head of state

indicators.note: in places that letter inside the other word

parts.note: really is an intensifier meaning very much

indicators.note: first to asks for the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A head of state who insists on being first to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: Regally means in the manner of a king or queen, a monarch being a head of state.

clue.text: Smoother way to dry ink once?

definitions.meaning: an abrasive sheet used to make wood smooth
sand and blotting paper were both once used to dry wet ink

explanation.surface: Asking whether a smoothing tool was an old method for drying ink.
explanation.walkthrough: Writers once sprinkled sand on wet ink or pressed paper on it; the second reading is whimsical, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: This abrasive sheet smooths surfaces, and its two halves name old ways of drying ink.

clue.text: Prefer to stay upright? Unbelievable

definitions.meaning: someone who would object to stooping would prefer to stay upright
so astonishing as to strain belief

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to bow and an onlooker finds it astonishing.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the hyphenated answer as two words: to object to stooping is to prefer staying upright.
explanation.definitionFit: Mind-bending describes ideas so strange they are hard to grasp or credit.

clue.text: Main layer of coal unfinished

indicators.note: unfinished says the last letter is lost

parts.note: a seam is a layer of coal in a mine

explanation.surface: A main coal layer left only partly mined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' looks like the adjective chief; here it is the old poetic noun for the open ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is a literary term for the ocean, as in the Spanish Main.

clue.text: Tubercular girl caught by Impressionist

parts.note: Mimi is the consumptive heroine of Puccini's opera La Bohème
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A sickly young woman was painted by one of the French Impressionist artists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Impressionist' looks like a painter such as Monet; here it means someone who does impressions.
explanation.definitionFit: An impressionist entertainer copies other people's voices and manners, which is exactly what a copycat performer does.

clue.text: Construction set a number short ——some prayers locate it

indicators.note: short means lacking, so the number is taken off

parts.note: Meccano is a classic metal construction toy

explanation.surface: A toy construction kit found missing a piece, with some praying to find it.
explanation.walkthrough: Muslims face towards the holy city when they pray, so prayers locate it.
explanation.definitionFit: Muslim prayer is directed towards this holy city in Saudi Arabia, so worshippers fix its direction.

clue.text: Innards of organ to me sounding less interesting

indicators.note: sounding says the next word is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: duller means more boring, less interesting

explanation.surface: Someone finds a church organ's inner workings boring.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent duller ends like DULLA.
explanation.definitionFit: The medulla is the inner core of an organ such as the kidney, as opposed to its cortex.

clue.text: Show emotion, about to deal with supplier

indicators.note: about says the first word goes round the second

parts.note: to cry is to shed tears
to handle a matter is to deal with it

explanation.surface: Someone gets emotional while about to trade with a supplier.
explanation.definitionFit: A chandlery is a business stocking provisions for ships, a ship's supplier.

clue.text: Perhaps brain working — there's a lot of logic to that

definitions.text: there's a lot of logic to that

parts.note: the brain is an example of a bodily organ, hence perhaps
a machine that is working is switched on

explanation.surface: Someone praising a working brain as a thing full of reason.
explanation.walkthrough: The Organon is the collected logical treatises of Aristotle.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristotle's Organon is a body of writings devoted wholly to logic, so it contains a great deal of it.

clue.text: A tyre finally fails, holding maximum speed in rural area

indicators.note: holding says one piece is placed inside the other
finally fails means the last letter of the tyre word drops away

parts.note: a radial is a common kind of car tyre
c is the physicist's symbol for the speed of light, the greatest speed possible

explanation.surface: A puncture on a country drive at top speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally fails' cuts the last letter from RADIAL to leave RADIA, and 'holding' puts C inside it; A goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcadia, a region of Greece, became the poetic byword for an idyllic countryside.

clue.text: Advice about extremely unusual cause of mania once

indicators.note: about says the advice word goes round the other letters

parts.note: a tip is a piece of useful advice

indicators.note: extremely asks for the outermost letters of the word unusual

explanation.surface: A warning against unusual advice that may have driven someone mad.
explanation.walkthrough: The mania is the tulip mania of seventeenth-century Holland, when bulbs sold for fortunes.
explanation.definitionFit: Speculation in these bulbs caused a famous financial frenzy in the 1630s Netherlands, hence a cause of mania long ago.

clue.text: Revealed to be full of salt that's encrusted

indicators.note: to be full of means the first word contains the second

parts.note: bared means uncovered or revealed
NaCl is the chemical formula of common salt, sodium chloride

explanation.surface: Something uncovered turns out to be caked with salt.
explanation.definitionFit: A hull covered in clinging shellfish is crusted over by them, so the adjective describes being encrusted.

clue.text: Tom's rough guide

definitions.meaning: the governance belonging to the tiny folk hero Tom Thumb
an approximate practical method based on experience

explanation.surface: Someone named Tom wrote a rough travel guidebook.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom Thumb is the thumb-sized hero of English folklore; his reign would be the rule of Thumb.
explanation.definitionFit: A rule of thumb is an approximate practical principle, a rough guide rather than exact calculation.

clue.text: A major say in explanation

definitions.meaning: A major is an example of a musical tonality, hence say
a ... is something that explains, like the ... to a map or puzzle

explanation.surface: Someone with a big influence on how a matter is explained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'major say' reads like an important voice; split it as A major, a musical key, with say meaning for example.
explanation.definitionFit: A key in music is a tonality like A major; a key to a code or map is its explanation.

clue.text: Initial impetus sharp, but excitement's over

indicators.note: over places the excitement word above the other in this down entry

parts.note: kicks are thrills, and the 's supplies the final letter
tart means sharp in taste

explanation.surface: A sharp beginning, after which the thrill is gone.
explanation.definitionFit: A kick-start is a boost that gets something going, just as kicking a motorcycle's pedal starts its engine.

clue.text: Last but one minute in an elite — put out

indicators.note: in places the minute letter inside the rearranged letters
out signals the letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: A latecomer, second to last, is put out of an elite group at the final minute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges AN ELITE PUT into PENULTIATE, and 'in' puts M inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Penultimate is the standard word for the one before the final item in a series.

clue.text: Set off eating — it's cooked

indicators.note: cooked suggests these letters have been doctored or rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook announcing a meal is ready and starting to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: To instigate something is to trigger or start it.

clue.text: Bed obscuring front of buggy that's occupying the same space

parts.note: a cot is a small bed, especially a child's

indicators.note: the bed hides the opening letter of the next word so it is lost

parts.note: buggy, meaning infested with bugs, is verminous

explanation.surface: A cot parked so that it blocks the front of a pushchair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buggy' looks like a pushchair; it is the adjective for bug-ridden, and 'obscuring front of' says the bed covers up its opening letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Coterminous means having the same boundaries, so two such areas occupy exactly the same space.

clue.text: Advert that's on the back of the cab

definitions.meaning: a preview shown to promote a film

definitions.text: on the back of the cab
definitions.meaning: the wheeled unit hitched behind a lorry's cab

explanation.surface: An advertisement displayed on the rear of a taxi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cab' suggests a taxi; it is the driver's cab of an articulated lorry.
explanation.definitionFit: A film preview is a promotional clip, and the towed unit behind a lorry cab bears the same name.

clue.text: Christopher and Elizabeth Cook

definitions.meaning: the surname shared by playwright Christopher ... and prison reformer Elizabeth ...
to cook in hot fat in a pan

explanation.surface: Two people named Christopher and Elizabeth Cook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' looks like their shared surname; it is a verb, and the surname wanted is another.
explanation.definitionFit: Both famous people bore this surname, and the word is also a verb for cooking in a pan.

clue.text: Member of union free to dip into money in till without end

indicators.note: to dip into says one word goes inside another
without end says the final letter goes

parts.note: a float is the cash put in a till for giving change
to rid is to free of something

explanation.surface: A trade union member is free to help themselves to the shop's takings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member of union' suggests a trade unionist; the union is the United States, and the member one of its states.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the fifty states that make up the federal union of the USA.

clue.text: Road surface half visible in delicate, faint glow

indicators.note: visible in says the shortened surface shows inside the other word

parts.note: slight means frail or delicate

indicators.note: half keeps only the first three of the six letters

parts.note: tarmac is the usual British word for a paved road surface

explanation.surface: A road surface glimpsed faintly in the gentle glow of the stars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' keeps only the first half of the road surface word, and 'visible in' places that inside the word for delicate.
explanation.definitionFit: Light from the stars is a pale, dim illumination at night, hence a faint glow.

clue.text: Let out from jail, finally become less violent

clue.text: One's holding a party for people one reveres

parts.note: one is I as a Roman numeral, and the 's is IS

explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' is read as 'one is', giving I + IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Icons are idolised figures, heroes held up for admiration and worship.

clue.text: A number, about a million, died here

indicators.note: about says the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: some means an unspecified number

explanation.surface: A grim tally: about a million soldiers died in this place.
explanation.walkthrough: The Battle of the Somme in 1916 left over a million casualties.

clue.text: Very attentive, but too short to land major acting role?

indicators.note: to land means to catch and hold, so the shortened word takes in the role
short says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: also means too or as well

explanation.definitionFit: Someone listening intently is said in an idiom to be nothing but listening organs, paying full attention.

clue.text: What the Sun regularly does is conventional

explanation.definitionFit: The sun sinks below the horizon daily, and the same word means fixed or customary.
